sources.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Building a Stronger and Fairer Super System) Act 2026 (Act No. 8, 2026)
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026: Register status: In force; assented to 13 March 2026. Inserts Division 296 into the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997. Section 296-30: large superannuation balance threshold $3,000,000 for 2026-27, indexed from 2027-28. Section 296-35: very large threshold $10,000,000 for 2026-27, indexed from 2027-28. Section 296-40: proportion is (reference amount less threshold) over reference amount times 100, rounded to 2 decimal places. Transitional section 296-1: applies to 2026-27 and later years; for 2026-27 only the TSB at the end of the year is used, and no liability arises if the person dies on or before the last day of 2026-27. Section 296-130: assessed tax is due 84 days after notice unless deferred to a Division 296 debt account.
sources.limitations: The rates are in the separate imposition Act (next record). Commencement table detail was not fully captured. Verify the compiled text for the year at use time.

sources.title: Superannuation (Building a Stronger and Fairer Super System) Imposition Act 2026 (Act No. 9, 2026)
sources.fact: Read by an agent on 24 September 2026; not yet reviewed by a person. Assented to 13 March 2026. Imposes tax payable under section 296-15 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997. The amount is 15% of taxable superannuation earnings, or, where the person has a very large superannuation balance earnings component, 15% of taxable superannuation earnings plus 10% of that component. Tax is not imposed where imposing it would exceed the legislative power of the Commonwealth.
sources.limitations: Read from the as-made text; section numbers for the rate provision were not captured. Verify the compiled text for the year at use time.

sources.title: ATO: How Division 296 tax is calculated
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 29 June 2026): 15% tax on total super earnings for the proportion of the TSB reference amount over the large threshold, and an additional 10% on earnings for the proportion over the very large threshold. Limited recourse borrowing arrangement amounts are never included in TSB for Division 296. Funds report relevant super earnings; SMSFs report through the SMSF annual return.
sources.limitations: The page's Leanne example multiplies $4,072.65 by '5%' but states $610.90, which is 15%; the worked figure matches the 15% rule. The ATO says it is drafting a law companion ruling on fund earnings. Verify the complete page at use time.
